datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: MasakhaPOS, MasakhaNER-X, MasakhaNEWS created from African language news articles (Section 3.2.1-3.2.2). AfriSenti and AfriHate from African language tweets (Section 3.2.1). NollySenti from Nigerian movie reviews. AfriQA has questions natively authored in African languages (Section 3.2.4). AfriADR derived from African language text in MAFAND (Section 3.2.5).

datasets_translated_from_english.evidence: SIB-200 based on FLORES English sentences. AfriXNLI translated from English XNLI (Adelani et al., 2024b). Belebele translated from English (Bandarkar et al., 2024). Uhura-Arc-Easy described as 'human-translated version of the scientific Arc-Easy benchmark' (Section 3.2.4). AfriMMLU and OpenAI-MMMLU are 'human-translated MMLU datasets' (Section 3.2.4). AfriMGSM is 'extension of the MGSM dataset' translated from English. FLORES-200: 'All translations are from English' (Section 3.2.5). NTREX-128 translated from English news references.

details.MasakhaPOS: Created from African language news articles
details.MasakhaNER-X: Named entities from African language texts
details.AfriSenti: Tweets natively authored in African languages
details.AfriHate: Tweets in African languages reflecting local hate speech patterns
details.AfriADR: Diacritics restoration for African languages — an inherently culture/language-specific task

all_annotators_native_speakers.evidence: Datasets from the Masakhane community (MasakhaPOS, MasakhaNER-X, MasakhaNEWS, AfriSenti, AfriHate, MAFAND) likely involved native speakers. AfriADR was automatically generated. Translated datasets (FLORES, Belebele, etc.) used professional translators whose nativeness is not confirmed in this paper.

annotator_workforce.evidence: AfroBench authors are from Masakhane NLP, Mila, McGill University, University of Waterloo, UCL, The African Research Collective, and Lelapa AI. The paper aggregates existing datasets from Masakhane community and other organizations. No ethics statement section is present in the paper. No annotator compensation or IRB details are reported.

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: The benchmark explicitly addresses English-centricity concerns. Section 5.2 reports 'Large gap in performance when compared to English' — GPT-4o and Gemini-1.5 pro achieve average scores better than Gemma 2 27B by over 20 points on African languages. Open models show 25-40 point gaps compared to English (Section 1). However, 9 of 22 datasets are translated from English, and the benchmark uses English prompts for evaluation (cross-lingual prompting approach, Appendix H). Several knowledge-intensive tasks (MMLU, Arc-Easy, MGSM) test Western-centric knowledge translated into African languages.

notably_excluded: Most of North Africa has only Arabic dialect representation
No indigenous American, Asian, European, or Oceanian languages
geographic_representation.evidence: Section 3.1: 'We cover 64 African languages from seven language families (Afro-Asiatic, Atlantic-Congo, Austronesian, Indo-European, Mande, Nilotic, and English-Creole). 40 languages are from the Atlantic-Congo family, 12 from the Afro-Asiatic family, seven from the Nilotic family, 2 Indo-European, 2 Creole languages, and 1 Austronesian language.' Table 10 shows languages span West, East, Southern, Central, and North Africa.
